review_history.resolution: Require strict optional equality in all checkpoint APIs; defined-to-undefined and undefined-to-defined transitions invalidate existing rows and use the established refold path. Add explicit registry and cache integration cases.

review_history.finding: The previous ambiguity is closed by strict optional cacheFingerprint equality for persisted rows and definitions in both directions.

scope: REM-028-S014: active visible agent-instructions baseline lookup
REM-028-S015: active visible agent-instructions duplicate check
REM-028-S016: active visible agent-instructions change fold
REM-028-S018: loaded and created-session time-context invariant replay

current_reader_observations.observation: Claimed authority messages are searched newest-first before active Session surface messages; the history lookup only needs the latest active baseline source.
Duplicate detection compares a desired UserMessage against claimed messages or active surface user messages by exact content and source.
Visible instruction changes fold active surface user messages in order, with later scope changes overwriting earlier values before claimed authority messages are applied.
The reverse scan takes raw user messages after the matching turn/start and appends proposed messages; the already-registered timeContext unit tracks durable message and injection times.

Startup and session/created validation replay every package-owned reading against its preceding durable prefix; session/created now supplies the exact SessionCreationBaseline, including unpublished accepted appends.
The internal/dispatch hook validates a candidate synchronously before Session.append mutates the log, currently by snapshotting the complete prefix.

behavioral_distinctions: Agent-instructions uses the active visible surface; compacted or replaced hidden messages must not affect its current baseline or change state.
Time-context uses the raw current-turn event suffix; user messages shadowed by compaction still contribute browser-zone facts and must remain included.
Invalid clientTimeZone values may be durably appended today; they throw only when an eligible time-context read derives browser policy or when a durable time-context reading is validated.
Time-context invariant failure before append leaves Session.seq and its event log unchanged; synchronous session/created failure rolls back SessionStore publication.

agent_instructions.decision: Use Session.deriveMessages() at each reader's current decision point. Search its user-role messages in reverse for the latest active baseline, compare desired messages against its active user-role messages, and fold active instruction changes in forward surface order. Apply claimed and authority-message precedence in the current order.
preserved_behavior: Active surface replacement and compaction determine which durable instruction messages contribute; hidden older messages do not reappear in visible change state.
Claimed and authority messages retain priority and ordering relative to the durable active surface.
Exact duplicate comparison continues to use deep equality of both content and source.
No instruction prose, new Session projection key, or arbitrary historical reader is introduced.
falsifying_cases: The newest active compatible baseline wins after replacement and resume.
Compaction that hides a baseline or nested change causes the same re-arm or reconciliation currently observed from active surface nodes.
An identical active user message prevents a duplicate inbox entry; a source or content difference does not.
Claimed messages continue to override or precede active history exactly as the current loops specify.

time_context_projection.decision: Extend the existing host-only timeContext projection rather than use Session.deriveMessages(). Raise its stateVersion from 2 to 3. Keep the existing lastMessageTime, lastInjectionTime, and lastTurnInjectionTime folds, and add the open turn/step/request-header position plus ordered unique raw browser-zone inputs folded from committed user events.
state_facts: openTurn, openStep, and requestStarted mirror preparationPosition's turn/start, step/start, request/header, step/end, and turn/end transitions.

browserTimeZoneInputs stores ordered unique raw clientTimeZone strings from user-rpc messages after the current turn/start. It does not classify or canonicalize them during the event fold; it resets at turn/start and turn/end.

firstValidationFailure stores the first invalid durable time-context reading diagnostic across the complete Session history so a late invariant registration can fail without rescanning Session events. It does not reject an ordinary invalid user message.

timeContext registers an exact cacheFingerprint derived from the Node, V8, ICU, CLDR, and time-zone database versions used for browser-zone validation and timestamp formatting. Same-key projection registrations must agree exactly on both stateVersion and optional cacheFingerprint; a definition that adds, removes, or changes a fingerprint cannot silently share another unit's fold.
A new internal projection module owns the JSON schema and shared event transition/reading validation helpers used by the main plugin and invariant companion; the module is not a package export.
time_context_projection.request_derivation: When injection is due, derive policy from the stored raw entered-turn values followed by browser-zone values in decision.messages in their existing order. Validate all values through the existing Intl-based canonicalization at read time, then sort and deduplicate valid zones and preserve mixed/missing output. This keeps each runtime's current support and canonicality decisions, including first-error order. Do not derive zones for a rejected or already-aborted decision, and do not parse stored values on the positive-interval early return.
preserved_behavior: Compaction and surface replacement do not remove raw user events from the browser-zone policy for the open turn.
The first invalid entered zone precedes all proposed messages; otherwise proposed-zone errors retain their input order.
Invalid zone data remains appendable and the error remains delayed until a time-context read or durable reading validation needs it.

A timeContext checkpoint from another Intl environment has a different cacheFingerprint and is discarded; the complete event log is refolded under the current environment before request state or the invariant latch is used.
The latest durable time-context injection remains counted even when its event is shadowed; interval and elapsed-time behavior is unchanged.
Turn start/end reset only the open-turn summary and existing lastTurnInjectionTime; lastMessageTime and lastInjectionTime retain their current folds.
time_context_projection.cache_compatibility: The state remains host-only plain JSON and does not alter SessionEventMap, SESSION_FORMAT_VERSION, released Session records, persistence SCHEMA_VERSION, SDK output, or provider request fields. Version-2 timeContext checkpoint rows are unusable under version 3. Add optional cacheFingerprint metadata to ProjectionDefinition and ProjectionCheckpointRow. Projection row eligibility is exact across checkpoint, viewCheckpoint, restoreFloor, and restore: a row is usable only when stateVersion matches and row.cacheFingerprint === definition.cacheFingerprint, using strict optional equality (both absent or the exact same string). Adding, removing, or changing a definition fingerprint makes existing rows unusable; in particular, a row with a fingerprint and a current definition without one follows the same mismatch invalidation/refold path. Definitions without a fingerprint remain compatible with rows that also omit it. Re-registering a key requires exact equality of both stateVersion and optional cacheFingerprint, including undefined-versus-defined mismatches. timeContext fingerprints Node, V8, ICU, CLDR, and time-zone database versions. A mismatch follows the existing version-mismatch path: restoreFloor selects seq 0, a complete-log restore starts from init, and a tail-only restore requests a seq-0 reread. Matching metadata leaves each API's existing schema-invalid behavior unchanged: viewCheckpoint omits the row, direct registry restore rejects it, prepared hydration retries with the exact baseline, and a malformed persisted record is backed up and skipped by the cache domain. The cache row schema accepts an absent optional fingerprint, so the projection-cache domain remains at version 7; a v7 archived on-disk fixture must prove compatibility and refold behavior. This refreshes raw-zone derivation and firstValidationFailure under current Intl behavior without weakening corruption handling.

time_context_invariant.decision: Share the timeContext event fold with the invariant. During installation, validate current Sessions from the projection's latched first validation failure; fail loudly if the timeContext projection is missing or lacks an exact cell. During session/created, replay and validate the supplied SessionCreationBaseline.events in sequence. During internal/dispatch, synchronously validate the candidate against sessionProjections.stateOf(session, 'timeContext') before commit, without mutating the prefix state. The cacheFingerprint ensures the latch was folded under the current Node/V8/ICU/CLDR/time-zone database environment; a mismatch requires full-log refold before the latch can be read.
preserved_behavior: A malformed, misplaced, wrong-zone, or otherwise invalid reading still fails before Session.append changes seq or log contents.
A bad constructor or setup prefix still throws synchronously from session/created and rolls the SessionStore attach back.
Late invariant installation still rejects an invalid existing Session and accepts a valid one when the timeContext projection has maintained the same event history.
After an Intl environment change, the historical validation latch is rebuilt from the exact log; a stale prior-runtime error or success is never trusted.
Fork, resume, and restore rebuild position, zone facts, and the validation latch from the exact SessionCreationBaseline; no parent Agent cache is inherited.
falsifying_cases: A rejected candidate leaves Session.seq, snapshotEvents(), and the projection watermark unchanged; the same corrected event can then append.
Creation validation includes accepted unpublished setup appends and rejects before SessionStore publication.
A late valid and late invalid invariant registration match current replay outcomes without calling eventAt or snapshotEvents.
A forked or resumed open turn retains raw browser-zone facts, including facts whose messages compaction later shadows.

A v3 checkpoint carrying another Intl cacheFingerprint is rejected by the existing version/fingerprint mismatch path and refolded from seq 0; the rebuilt state reclassifies raw zones and durable readings under current Intl behavior.
An aborted or rejected pre-step performs no time-context derivation and appends no reading.

required_verification: Focused agent-instructions, time-context, and time-context-invariant package tests, including Session.append rejection and created-session rollback.

Projection restore/hydrate from an old timeContext stateVersion 2 row refolds the exact complete event log and produces version 3 state; retain the existing session-projection and cache version-mismatch fallback tests.

A same-stateVersion checkpoint with a mismatched Intl cacheFingerprint follows the existing mismatch path: restoreFloor selects seq 0, full-log restore refolds under current Intl behavior, and tail-only restore requires a full-log reread. Verify the cache integration serializes and rejects environment-mismatched rows. Preserve per-reader schema-invalid behavior: viewCheckpoint omits a unit row, direct registry restore rejects it, prepared hydration retries from the exact baseline, and malformed stored records use backup-and-skip.

Verify same-key registry registration permits matching optional cacheFingerprint values and rejects a different fingerprint or defined-versus-undefined mismatch; update duplicate-key JSDoc and the generated Cordis catalog.

Verify persisted rows with a defined cacheFingerprint become unusable when a same-stateVersion definition removes its fingerprint: viewCheckpoint omits the row, restoreFloor selects seq 0, and full restore starts from init and refolds. Verify tail-only restore requires a seq-0 reread. Cover the reverse defined-versus-undefined transition and matching-fingerprint control in registry and cache integration cases.

Add a real archived v7 on-disk cache fixture without cacheFingerprint and prove the optional row schema still opens it and the registry refolds environment-bound rows from the complete log; projection-cache domain version remains 7.

Run the unmodified turn-outline, session-title, and token-meter projection cases that require schema-invalid rows with matching metadata to keep throwing; the environment fingerprint path must not change corruption semantics.
Raw browser-zone inputs hidden by compaction remain effective after resume and fork; keep invalid-zone delayed failure and input-order assertions.
Scoped package typechecks and lint; verify-type-equiv, verify-cordis-catalog, export-JSDoc, package dependency, active reader count, and owned invariant checks.
Paired README and session-projection documentation validation, translation pairing, doc-typecheck/doc-quick coverage, and whitespace checks.

No model-visible wording or ordering changes are intended; existing time-context request/history assertions remain the output oracle, with snapshot updates only if those assertions expose an actual output change.

criteria: A21-01: S014-S016 use the active model-visible message projection while retaining surface, ordering, authority, and exact deduplication semantics.
A21-02: S017 uses raw-event-equivalent current-turn facts, including compaction-shadowed events, and retains delayed invalid-zone failures and proposed-message order.
A21-03: S018 validates the exact creation baseline and late existing-session status without complete-history Session reads.
A21-04: S019 remains synchronous before append commit and rejects without changing the durable cursor or log.
A21-05: Restore, resume, fork, setup append, cancellation, and missing projection state have explicit exact behavior.

A21-06: Version-2 rows and same-version Intl-environment-mismatched rows are discarded and refolded from seq 0 through exact stateVersion and optional cacheFingerprint equality, including both defined-to-undefined and undefined-to-defined mismatches. Schema-invalid rows with matching metadata retain their existing per-reader behavior. No Session format, persistence schema, wire, SDK, or model-visible change occurs.

A21-07: The implementation path list includes owning package documentation, bilingual pairing metadata, generated Cordis catalog/type compatibility output, raw-zone helper tests, projection/cache fingerprint compatibility tests, and the archived v7 cache fixture required by the cache schema rule.
